title: The static keyword in Java
answer: `static` associates a member with the class rather than with each object instance. Static fields hold shared class-level state, static methods can be called without an instance and cannot directly use instance state, and static initialization runs when the class is initialized. AeroTopo's `LanguageLab` shows static final constants, a mutable static counter, a static block, and static utility methods alongside the non-static `accepted` field, making the ownership difference visible.
